🔄 Appendix E: Data Science Pipeline YAML TemplatesReference

5-Step ML Pipeline for anihpj Job Classification

Complete Kubeflow Pipelines (kfp) SDK components for the anihpj data science pipeline — from S3 data ingestion through preprocessing, training, evaluation, and model export. Each component is a self-contained Python function that runs as a containerized pipeline step.

📋 Reference⏱️ ~20 minEX267 30%
🧑‍🏫 Novice's Corner — "What's a Pipeline Component?"

A pipeline component is a self-contained Python function decorated with @dsl.component. Each component runs in its own container with its own dependencies, inputs, and outputs. Data flows between components as artifacts (files stored in S3/MinIO). This means your ingestion step can use Pandas while your training step uses PyTorch — they don't share a Python environment. The dsl.Input[dsl.Dataset] and dsl.Output[dsl.Dataset] annotations tell Kubeflow how to wire components together. Think of it as LEGO blocks for ML workflows — each block does one thing, and you snap them together to build a pipeline.

🔄 anihpj 5-Step Pipeline Flow
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│ E.1      │    │ E.2      │    │ E.3      │    │ E.4      │    │ E.5      │
│ INGEST   │───▶│PREPROCESS│───▶│  TRAIN   │───▶│ EVALUATE │───▶│  EXPORT  │
│          │    │          │    │          │    │          │    │          │
│S3→CSV    │    │Skills→   │    │XGBoost   │    │accuracy  │    │Model→S3  │
│validate  │    │features   │    │fit+predict│   │F1+report │    │+metadata │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘
     │               │               │               │               │
  Dataset         Dataset          Model          Markdown        S3 URI
  (CSV)           (CSV)         (joblib)         (report)     (s3://...)

E.1 Data Ingestion Component

Python — kfp Component: Ingest from S3📋
from kfp import dsl, components

@dsl.component(
    base_image="registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/python-311",
    packages_to_install=["boto3", "pandas", "sqlalchemy"]
)
def ingest_data(
    s3_bucket: str,
    s3_key: str,
    output_path: dsl.Output[dsl.Dataset]
):
    import boto3, pandas as pd
    s3 = boto3.client("s3")
    obj = s3.get_object(Bucket=s3_bucket, Key=s3_key)
    df = pd.read_csv(obj["Body"])
    # Clean + validate
    df = df.dropna(subset=["title", "description"])
    df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Ingested {len(df)} job postings")

E.2 Preprocessing Component (Skill Extraction)

Python — kfp Component: Feature Engineering📋
@dsl.component(
    base_image="registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/python-311",
    packages_to_install=["pandas", "scikit-learn", "nltk"]
)
def preprocess_features(
    input_data: dsl.Input[dsl.Dataset],
    preprocessed_data: dsl.Output[dsl.Dataset]
):
    import pandas as pd, re, nltk
    nltk.download("stopwords")
    from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

    df = pd.read_csv(input_data.path)
    # Extract skills from description
    skills = ["python", "java", "docker", "kubernetes", "aws", "azure"]
    for skill in skills:
        df[f"skill_{skill}"] = df["description"].str.contains(
            skill, case=False).astype(int)
    df["text_length"] = df["description"].str.len()
    df.to_csv(preprocessed_data.path, index=False)
    print(f"Preprocessed: {df.shape[1]} features created")

E.3 Training Component (XGBoost)

Python — kfp Component: Train + Metrics📋
@dsl.component(
    base_image="registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/python-311",
    packages_to_install=["pandas", "scikit-learn", "joblib", "xgboost"]
)
def train_model(
    preprocessed_data: dsl.Input[dsl.Dataset],
    model_output: dsl.Output[dsl.Model],
    metrics_output: dsl.Output[dsl.Metrics]
):
    import pandas as pd, joblib
    from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
    from xgboost import XGBClassifier
    from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score

    df = pd.read_csv(preprocessed_data.path)
    X = df.drop(columns=["title", "description", "category"])
    y = df["category"]
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.2)

    model = XGBClassifier(n_estimators=100, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1)
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)

    joblib.dump(model, model_output.path)
    metrics_output.metadata["accuracy"] = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
    metrics_output.metadata["f1"] = f1_score(y_test, y_pred, average="weighted")

E.4 Evaluation Component

Python — kfp Component: Evaluate + Report📋
@dsl.component(
    base_image="registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/python-311",
    packages_to_install=["pandas", "scikit-learn", "joblib", "matplotlib"]
)
def evaluate_model(
    preprocessed_data: dsl.Input[dsl.Dataset],
    model_input: dsl.Input[dsl.Model],
    eval_report: dsl.Output[dsl.Markdown]
):
    import pandas as pd, joblib
    from sklearn.metrics import classification_report

    df = pd.read_csv(preprocessed_data.path)
    model = joblib.load(model_input.path)
    X = df.drop(columns=["title", "description", "category"])
    y_true = df["category"]
    y_pred = model.predict(X)

    report = classification_report(y_true, y_pred)
    eval_report.path.write_text(f"# Model Evaluation\n\n```\n{report}\n```")

E.5 Model Export Component

Python — kfp Component: Export to S3📋
@dsl.component(
    base_image="registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/python-311",
    packages_to_install=["boto3", "joblib"]
)
def export_model(
    model_input: dsl.Input[dsl.Model],
    s3_bucket: str,
    model_name: str,
    version: str
):
    import boto3, joblib, json
    from datetime import datetime

    s3 = boto3.client("s3")
    key = f"{model_name}/v{version}/model.joblib"
    s3.upload_file(model_input.path, s3_bucket, key)

    metadata = {
        "model": model_name, "version": version,
        "exported_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        "s3_uri": f"s3://{s3_bucket}/{key}"
    }
    s3.put_object(Bucket=s3_bucket,
        Key=f"{model_name}/v{version}/metadata.json",
        Body=json.dumps(metadata))
    print(f"Model exported: s3://{s3_bucket}/{key}")
🚀 EX267 Tip: Pipeline Component Checklist

When creating a pipeline on the exam: 1) Define each component with @dsl.component, 2) Specify base_image (always use UBI), 3) Declare packages_to_install, 4) Use typed inputs/outputs (dsl.Input[dsl.Dataset]), 5) Wire them together in a @dsl.pipeline function. The pipeline UI in OpenShift AI auto-generates the DAG visualization from your Python code.

Python — How to Wire All 5 Components Into One Pipeline📋
from kfp import dsl

@dsl.pipeline(
    name="anihpj-job-classifier-pipeline",
    description="End-to-end job classification pipeline"
)
def anihpj_pipeline(
    s3_bucket: str = "anihpj-data",
    s3_key: str = "raw/job_postings.csv",
    model_name: str = "job-classifier",
    version: str = "2"
):
    # Wire components together — outputs flow to inputs
    ingest_task = ingest_data(s3_bucket=s3_bucket, s3_key=s3_key)
    preprocess_task = preprocess_features(
        input_data=ingest_task.outputs["output_path"])
    train_task = train_model(
        preprocessed_data=preprocess_task.outputs["preprocessed_data"])
    eval_task = evaluate_model(
        preprocessed_data=preprocess_task.outputs["preprocessed_data"],
        model_input=train_task.outputs["model_output"])
    export_task = export_model(
        model_input=train_task.outputs["model_output"],
        s3_bucket=s3_bucket, model_name=model_name, version=version)

# Compile to YAML for OpenShift AI:
# kfp dsl compile --py pipeline.py --output pipeline.yaml

🚀 Appendix F: Model Serving TemplatesReference

KServe & ModelMesh YAML Blueprints

Production-ready YAML templates for every model serving scenario on OpenShift AI — single-model KServe, multi-model ModelMesh, GPU inference, canary deployments, and autoscaling. Copy, customize, deploy.

📋 Reference⏱️ ~20 minEX267 25%
🧑‍🏫 Novice's Corner — "Which serving method should I use?"

KServe Serverless (KPA) is best for 1-5 models with variable traffic — it scales to zero when idle, saving GPU costs. ModelMesh is best for 10+ models with sporadic traffic — many models share one GPU pool. GPU inference adds nvidia.com/gpu: 1 to resources and nodeSelector to target GPU nodes. Canary deployments let you test a new model version with 10% of traffic before full rollout. Pick the template below that matches your scenario.

F.1 Single-Model KServe InferenceService

YAML — KServe Serverless Deployment📋
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: anihpj-job-classifier
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/deploymentMode: Serverless
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: sklearn
      storageUri: s3://anihpj-models/job-classifier/v2
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 500m, memory: 2Gi }
        limits: { cpu: 1, memory: 4Gi }
    minReplicas: 0       # Scale to zero when idle
    maxReplicas: 5
  transformer:           # Optional: pre/post-processing
    containers:
    - name: transformer
      image: quay.io/anihpj/preprocess:v1
      env:
      - name: MODEL_TYPE
        value: "classification"

F.2 Multi-Model ModelMesh ServingRuntime

YAML — ServingRuntime for ModelMesh📋
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: triton-multi-model
spec:
  supportedModelFormats:
  - name: sklearn
  - name: xgboost
  - name: pytorch
  containers:
  - name: triton
    image: nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:24.01-py3
    args:
    - tritonserver
    - --model-repository=s3://anihpj-models/
    - --allow-grpc=true
    - --allow-http=true
    resources:
      requests: { cpu: 1, memory: 4Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 1 }
      limits: { cpu: 2, memory: 8Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 1 }

F.3 GPU-Enabled Inference YAML

YAML — KServe with GPU + NodeSelector + Tolerations📋
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: anihpj-skill-ranker-gpu
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat: { name: pytorch }
      storageUri: s3://anihpj-models/skill-ranker/
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
        memory: 16Gi
    nodeSelector:
      nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
    tolerations:
    - key: nvidia.com/gpu
      operator: Exists
      effect: NoSchedule

F.4 Canary Deployment Configuration

YAML — Canary: 10% Traffic to New Version📋
# Deploy v3 model alongside v2, route 10% traffic to it
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: anihpj-job-classifier-v3
spec:
  predictor:
    canaryTrafficPercent: 10      # 10% → v3, 90% → v2
    model:
      modelFormat: { name: sklearn }
      storageUri: s3://anihpj-models/job-classifier/v3

F.5 Autoscaler Configuration (KPA)

AnnotationValueWhat It Does
autoscaling.knative.dev/minScale"0"Scale to zero pods when idle (saves cost)
autoscaling.knative.dev/maxScale"5"Maximum 5 pods under peak load
autoscaling.knative.dev/target"10"10 concurrent requests per pod before scaling up
autoscaling.knative.dev/scaleDownDelay"60s"Wait 60 seconds before scaling down (prevents flapping)
autoscaling.knative.dev/window"30s"Averaging window for metrics (smooths spikes)
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: anihpj-job-classifier
  annotations:
    autoscaling.knative.dev/minScale: "0"
    autoscaling.knative.dev/maxScale: "5"
    autoscaling.knative.dev/target: "10"
    autoscaling.knative.dev/scaleDownDelay: "60s"
    autoscaling.knative.dev/window: "30s"
🧭 Serving Decision Flowchart — Which Method Should You Use?
How many models?
  ├── 1-5 models
  │   ├── Variable/sporadic traffic? → KServe Serverless (KPA scale-to-zero)
  │   └── Always-on, predictable? → KServe Raw (HPA) with minReplicas ≥ 1
  │
  ├── 10-50+ models
  │   └── ModelMesh (multi-model, GPU-efficient, LRU caching)
  │
  └── Need GPU?
      ├── Yes → Add nvidia.com/gpu: 1 + nodeSelector + tolerations
      ├── Need multi-GPU → NVIDIA Triton with instance groups
      └── CPU only → Standard KServe (sklearn, xgboost, etc.)

🔺 Appendix G: GPU Configuration Cheat SheetReference

Node Labels, Taints, MIG, Time-Slicing, nvidia-smi

Everything you need to configure, partition, and monitor NVIDIA GPUs on OpenShift — from node labels and taints through MIG profiles and DCGM diagnostics.

📋 Reference⏱️ ~20 minNCP-AII
🧑‍🏫 Novice's Corner — "Labels, Taints, Tolerations — what's the difference?"

Labels are like sticky notes on nodes — they describe what the node HAS (e.g., nvidia.com/gpu.product=A100). You use nodeSelector to say "run this pod ONLY on nodes with this label." Taints are like "KEEP OUT" signs — they repel pods that don't have the matching toleration. A GPU node tainted with nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule will reject all pods EXCEPT those with a toleration for that taint. This is how you make sure expensive GPU nodes only run AI workloads — not random web apps.

G.1 GPU Node Labels Quick Reference

LabelSet ByPurpose
nvidia.com/gpu.present=trueNFDAuto-detected GPU hardware presence
nvidia.com/gpu.count=4NFDNumber of GPUs on this node
nvidia.com/gpu.product=A100-SXM4-40GBNFDExact GPU model name
nvidia.com/gpu.memory=40960NFDVRAM in MB per GPU
nvidia.com/cuda.driver.major=535GPU OperatorCUDA driver version
nvidia.com/mig.capable=trueGPU OperatorMIG partitioning supported
feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0300_10de.present=trueNFDPCI device: 0300=GPU, 10de=NVIDIA

G.2 GPU Taints & Tolerations

Shell + YAML — Taint Nodes & Tolerate in Pods📋
# TAINT: Prevent non-GPU workloads from using expensive GPU nodes
oc adm taint node gpu-worker-1 nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule

# TOLERATION: Allow only AI workloads to run on GPU nodes
tolerations:
- key: nvidia.com/gpu
  operator: Equal
  value: "true"
  effect: NoSchedule

# NODESELECTOR: Pin GPU workloads to GPU nodes
nodeSelector:
  nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"

# COMBINED: Node affinity + toleration for production
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: nvidia.com/gpu.product
          operator: In
          values: ["A100-SXM4-40GB", "H100-PCIe-80GB"]

G.3 MIG Configuration Examples

🧩 MIG — Partitioning 1 Physical GPU into Multiple Virtual GPUs
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1× NVIDIA A100 40GB (Physical GPU)                               │
│  ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────┬──────┬────┐│
│  │ 1g.6gb   │ 1g.6gb   │ 1g.6gb   │ 1g.6gb   │2g.12g│2g.12g│3g. ││
│  │ 6GB VRAM │ 6GB VRAM │ 6GB VRAM │ 6GB VRAM │12GB  │12GB  │20GB││
│  │inference │inference │inference │inference │train │train │train││
│  └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────┴──────┴────┘│
│  Total: 7 isolated GPU instances from 1 A100                      │
│                                                                     │
│  1× NVIDIA H100 80GB (Physical GPU)                                │
│  ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──...──┐ │
│  │ 1g.12gb  │ 1g.12gb  │ 1g.12gb  │ 1g.12gb  │ 1g.12gb  │       │ │
│  │ 12GB     │ 12GB     │ 12GB     │ 12GB     │ 12GB     │ (x7)  │ │
│  │LLM infer │LLM infer │LLM infer │LLM infer │LLM infer │       │ │
│  └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
YAML — Enable MIG + View Instances📋
# Enable MIG in ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata: { name: gpu-cluster-policy }
spec:
  mig:
    strategy: mixed     # mixed | single | none
  migManager:
    enabled: true

# View MIG instances
nvidia-smi mig -lgi     # List GPU instances
nvidia-smi mig -lci     # List compute instances

G.4 GPU Time-Slicing Configuration

FeatureMIGTime-Slicing
IsolationHardware (VRAM + cache partitioned)Software (time multiplexing only)
VRAM guaranteeYes — dedicated VRAM per instanceNo — all share same VRAM pool
Error isolationYes — one instance crash doesn't affect othersNo — all share the GPU
GPU typesA100, A30, H100 onlyAll NVIDIA GPUs
Max instances7 per GPU (hardware limit)Unlimited (software config)
Best forProduction multi-tenantDev/test, inference burst
# Time-slicing ConfigMap: 1 GPU → 4 virtual GPUs
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: time-slicing-config
  namespace: nvidia-gpu-operator
data:
  default: |-
    version: v1
    sharing:
      timeSlicing:
        resources:
        - name: nvidia.com/gpu
          replicas: 4

🔴 Common GPU Issues
  • GPU not detected → NFD not installed
  • nvidia-smi fails → driver not loaded
  • Pod can't use GPU → SCC not privileged
  • MIG not working → strategy not "mixed"
  • OOM on GPU → model too large for VRAM
🟢 Quick Fixes
  • oc describe node | grep nvidia
  • oc debug node -- nvidia-smi
  • oc adm policy add-scc-to-user privileged
  • oc get clusterpolicy -o yaml | grep mig
  • Reduce batch size or use MIG for isolation

🚀 EX267 Strategy: Order Matters!

Always start with HIGH-weight tasks first (35% install, 30% pipelines, 25% serving). Low-weight monitoring tasks go last. If you run out of time, you've already secured 90% of available points. Never spend more than 15 minutes stuck on one task — flag it, move on, return at the end.

❌ Top 5 EX267 Mistakes
  • Using kubectl instead of oc (oc has AI commands)
  • Skipping post-task verification (always run health check)
  • Forgetting GPU node taints (CPU pods eat GPU nodes)
  • Not checking PVC status before launching notebooks
  • Using :latest image tags (breaks reproducibility)
✅ Top 5 Success Habits
  • Run alias setup script before any task
  • Verify every step: oc get → oc describe → oc logs
  • Use oc explain for any CRD you're unsure about
  • Always --dry-run=client -o yaml before applying
  • Submit SOMETHING for every task (partial credit!)

💻 Appendix I: Practice Lab Environment SetupReference

3 Ways to Get a Working OpenShift AI Lab

From local CRC to cloud sandbox — pick the option that fits your hardware and budget. Each option includes step-by-step setup and a validation checklist.

📋 Reference⏱️ ~30 minLab Setup
🧑‍🏫 Novice's Corner — "Which lab option is right for me?"

CRC (Option A) gives you a real OpenShift cluster on your laptop — full oc CLI, web console, everything. Best if you have 32GB+ RAM. Minikube (Option B) gives you a lightweight Kubernetes cluster with KServe + Pipelines but no OpenShift web console. Best for 16GB RAM machines. Cloud Sandbox (Option C) gives you a free managed OpenShift cluster with zero local setup — but limited to 7GB RAM and no GPU. Start with Option C if you just want to click through the console; graduate to Option A when you're ready for serious practice.

🔧 Appendix J: Troubleshooting FlowchartsReference

10 Decision Trees for Common EX267 Scenarios

When something breaks during the exam, don't panic — follow these decision trees. Each one starts with a symptom and guides you to the fix through a series of diagnostic commands.

📋 Reference⏱️ ~20 minTroubleshoot
🧑‍🏫 Novice's Corner — "How to use troubleshooting flowcharts"

Each flowchart follows the symptom → diagnostic → fix pattern. Start at the top, answer the question, follow the branch. The commands shown are exactly what you'd type in the terminal. Pro tip: On the EX267 exam, always run oc get pods and oc get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' first — these two commands solve 50% of problems before you even need a flowchart.

J.1 Notebook Won't Start

🌳 Notebook Won't Start — Decision Tree
Notebook pod status?
├── ImagePullBackOff → Wrong image? Private registry without pull secret?
│   Fix: oc describe pod → check image; oc create secret docker-registry
├── Pending (0/1 nodes) → No resources?
│   ├── No GPU? → oc describe node | grep nvidia
│   ├── Quota exceeded? → oc describe quota
│   └── PVC not bound? → oc get pvc → check StorageClass default
├── CrashLoopBackOff → OOMKilled?
│   Fix: Increase memory in Notebook CR → oc edit notebook <name>
└── Running but UI unreachable? → Route issue?
    Fix: oc get route -n <project> → check hostname

J.2 Pipeline Step Failure

🌳 Pipeline Step Failure — Decision Tree
Step pod status?
├── OOMKilled → oc describe pod → increase step memory in pipeline
├── Error (exit 1) → oc logs <step-pod>
│   ├── ImportError → Python dependency missing → add to requirements.txt
│   ├── PermissionError → S3 access denied → check Data Connection secret
│   └── KeyError → Wrong column name → data schema changed
├── Timeout → Increase timeout in pipeline step config
└── Evicted → Node disk pressure → oc adm top node

J.3 Model Serving Timeout

🌳 Model Serving Timeout — Decision Tree
curl endpoint → what happens?
├── 503 Service Unavailable → Cold start?
│   Fix: Wait 30-60s. OR set minReplicas=1 to prevent scale-to-zero
├── Connection Refused → Pod not running?
│   Check: oc get is → conditions → StorageNotAccessible? PredictorPending?
├── 504 Gateway Timeout → Model loading too slow?
│   Fix: Increase memory, check model size, pre-warm endpoint
└── 200 but high latency → Performance issue?
    Fix: Check GPU util (DCGM), add replicas, upgrade GPU

J.4 GPU Not Detected

🌳 GPU Not Detected — Decision Tree
oc describe node <gpu-node> | grep nvidia → labels present?
├── No labels → NFD not detecting GPU?
│   Fix: oc get pods -n node-feature-discovery → reinstall NFD
├── Labels present but pods pending → GPU Operator?
│   Check: oc get pods -n nvidia-gpu-operator → all Running?
│   Check: oc get clusterpolicy → created?
└── Labels + Operator OK → Pod can't use GPU?
    ├── SCC issue? → oc adm policy add-scc-to-user privileged -z default
    ├── Quota? → oc describe quota
    └── Taint not tolerated? → Add toleration to pod spec

J.5 PVC Mount Failure

🌳 PVC Mount Failure — Decision Tree
PVC status?
├── Pending → No default StorageClass?
│   Fix: oc patch sc <name> -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass...is-default":"true"}}}'
├── Bound but mount fails → Access mode mismatch?
│   ReadWriteOnce can only mount to 1 pod → use ReadWriteMany (RWX) for shared
└── Lost → PV deleted? → CSI snapshot restore if available

J.6 Operator Install Failure

🌳 Operator Install Failure — Decision Tree
oc get csv -n redhat-ods-operator → status?
├── Pending → InstallPlan not approved → oc get installplan → approve it
├── Failed → Dependency missing?
│   Check: oc get csv -A → all dependency operators Succeeded?
│   Common: Serverless Operator, Pipelines Operator, ServiceMesh
└── Succeeded but pods crashing → Insufficient resources
    Fix: Add worker nodes or increase node resources

J.7 Route Not Accessible

🌳 Route Not Accessible — Decision Tree
curl route → what happens?
├── DNS not resolving → Hostname not propagated? → Wait 5 min OR nslookup
├── Connection Refused → Service selector wrong?
│   Fix: oc describe svc <name> → verify selector matches pod labels
└── TLS cert error → Self-signed?
    Fix: oc create route edge --service=<name> --hostname=<fqdn>

J.8 Authentication Failure

🌳 Authentication Failure — Decision Tree
oc login fails?
├── "unauthorized" → Wrong credentials or expired token
│   Fix: oc login --token=<new-token> --server=<api-url>
├── "certificate signed by unknown authority" → Self-signed cluster
│   Fix: oc login --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true (dev only!)
└── OAuth pod not running → oc get pods -n openshift-authentication

J.9 Resource Quota Exceeded

🌳 Resource Quota Exceeded — Decision Tree
oc describe quota → which resource is exhausted?
├── CPU → Reduce requests OR increase quota
│   Fix: oc patch resourcequota <name> -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"cpu":"10"}}}'
├── Memory → Same as CPU
├── GPU (nvidia.com/gpu) → Free GPU by stopping unused notebooks
│   OR enable MIG/time-slicing to share GPUs
└── PVC count/storage → Delete unused PVCs or increase quota

J.10 OOM Kill (Out of Memory)

🌳 OOM Kill — Decision Tree
oc describe pod → State: OOMKilled
├── Training job? → Reduce batch size OR increase node memory
├── Inference? → Model too large → use smaller model OR add GPU memory
├── Data processing? → Process in chunks (Dask/Spark) instead of full dataset
└── Memory leak? → Check pod memory trend: oc adm top pod --containers
🔧 EX267 Troubleshooting Command Trinity — Memorize This!

80% of EX267 troubleshooting tasks are solved by these three commands in order: 1) oc get pods — what's running/not running? 2) oc describe <resource> — what happened? (check Events section) 3) oc logs <pod> --tail=50 — what did the app say? If these three don't solve it, then use the flowcharts above. Never start troubleshooting without running them first — the Events section of oc describe is the single most valuable piece of information in OpenShift debugging.

K.2 GPU Operator ClusterPolicy Reference

YAML — Complete ClusterPolicy📋
apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: gpu-cluster-policy
spec:
  operator:
    defaultRuntime: crio
    deployGFD: true          # GPU Feature Discovery
  driver:
    enabled: true
    version: "535.154.05"    # Pin driver version
    rdma:
      enabled: false         # Enable for InfiniBand
  toolkit: { enabled: true }
  devicePlugin:
    enabled: true
    config:
      name: time-slicing-config
  mig:
    strategy: mixed          # mixed | single | none
  migManager: { enabled: true }
  dcgmExporter: { enabled: true }   # Prometheus GPU metrics
  validator: { enabled: true }
  gfd: { enabled: true }            # GPU Feature Discovery labels

BuildConfigOpenShift CI/CD build definition — like a Dockerfile + builder config combined
ClusterOperatorManages cluster-level services (DNS, OAuth, monitoring, etc.)
ClusterVersionTracks and manages OpenShift version and updates
ConfigMapNon-sensitive key-value configuration injected into pods
CRCCodeReady Containers → OpenShift Local — single-node dev cluster
CSIContainer Storage Interface — storage driver plugin standard
DataScienceClusterCRD that configures all OpenShift AI components (DSC)
DeploymentManages rolling updates for stateless applications
ImageStreamOpenShift's image version tracking abstraction
MachineSetControls node scaling in cloud/VM clusters
ocOpenShift CLI — kubectl superset with OpenShift-specific commands
OLMOperator Lifecycle Manager — installs, manages, and updates operators
OperatorKubernetes-native application packager with operational knowledge
RBACRole-Based Access Control — who can do what in the cluster
RouteOpenShift's external access mechanism — like Ingress but more powerful
SCCSecurity Context Constraint — pod-level security policy (OpenShift-only)
SecretSensitive configuration data (passwords, tokens, keys)
ServiceStable internal network endpoint for pods
StatefulSetStateful app with stable pod identities and persistent storage
SubscriptionOLM resource linking an operator to its catalog source

L.2 AI/ML Terms (A-Z)

TermDefinition
AutoMLAutomated ML — Katib tunes hyperparameters automatically
Canary DeploymentGradual rollout of new model version (10%→50%→100% traffic)
Cold StartDelay when model loads from zero replicas (scale-to-zero)
Data DriftModel accuracy degrades because input data distribution changes
DDPPyTorch Distributed Data Parallel — multi-GPU training
ExplainerKServe container showing WHY a model made a prediction (SHAP/LIME)
Feature StoreCentralized repository for ML features (Feast)
HuggingFaceModel hub + transformers library — hf:// storageURI support
InferenceServiceKServe CRD representing a deployed model endpoint
KatibKubeflow hyperparameter tuning framework on OpenShift
KPAKnative Pod Autoscaler — scale-to-zero for inference endpoints
KServeStandard Kubernetes model serving framework
LLMLarge Language Model (GPT, LLaMA, Mistral, etc.)
MLflowML experiment tracking and model registry
ModelMeshMulti-model serving — many models share serving pods
OCI ArtifactModels packaged as container images (portable across registries)
RAGRetrieval-Augmented Generation — LLM + vector database
TensorRTNVIDIA inference optimization — 2-5× throughput improvement
vLLMHigh-throughput LLM serving with PagedAttention
WorkbenchOpenShift AI Jupyter notebook instance with GPU/PVC support

L.3 GPU & Hardware Terms (A-Z)

TermDefinition
A100NVIDIA Ampere GPU — 40/80GB HBM2e, 312 TFLOPS (FP16)
CUDA CoresGeneral-purpose GPU processing units
DCGMData Center GPU Manager — monitoring + diagnostics
DGXNVIDIA AI supercomputer — 8× A100/H100 in one chassis
ECCError-Correcting Code memory — protects GPU VRAM data integrity
GPUDirect RDMAGPU-to-GPU data transfer bypassing CPU memory
H100NVIDIA Hopper GPU — 80GB HBM3, 989 TFLOPS (FP8)
HBMHigh Bandwidth Memory — stacked GPU memory for high throughput
InfiniBandHigh-speed interconnect — 200-400 Gbps for GPU clusters
L40SNVIDIA Ada Lovelace — inference-optimized, 48GB VRAM
MIGMulti-Instance GPU — hardware partition of 1 GPU into up to 7 isolated instances
NCCLNVIDIA Collective Communications Library — multi-GPU training
NFDNode Feature Discovery — auto-labels nodes by hardware features
NVLinkHigh-speed GPU-to-GPU interconnect — 900 GB/s per link
nvidia-smiNVIDIA System Management Interface — GPU CLI tool
Tensor CoreSpecialized GPU unit for matrix multiplication (AI/ML)
Time-SlicingSoftware GPU sharing — time multiplexing between pods
TOPSTrillion Operations Per Second — AI performance metric
vGPUVirtual GPU — share GPU across virtual machines
VRAMVideo RAM — GPU memory for model weights, activations, batches

L.4 Exam Jargon Decoder

Exam PhraseWhat It Really Means
"Create a data science project"oc new-project OR web console → DS Project
"Configure a workbench"Create Notebook CR with custom image + PVC + GPU
"Set up a data connection"Create Secret + Data Connection config (S3/DB)
"Deploy a model"Create InferenceService CRD with storageUri
"Enable monitoring"ConfigMap: cluster-monitoring-config with user workload enabled
"Allocate GPU resources"Add nvidia.com/gpu: 1 to pod resource limits + nodeSelector + tolerations
"Create a pipeline"Use Elyra (UI) or kfp SDK (Python) with @dsl.component
"Register a model"Push model as OCI artifact to Model Registry with version tags
"Troubleshoot a failure"oc describe + oc logs + oc get events — the holy trinity
"Verify the installation"oc get dsc → all components show managementState: Managed
